feature: Avoid duplicate .count() queries in list views
workflow_rationale: Simple performance optimization affecting only 2 files with straightforward code changes. No architectural changes needed.

phases.name: Fix Duplicate COUNT Queries
phases.description: Replace queryset.count() calls with paginator.count in affected list views

subtasks.description: Fix material_list view - replace materials.count() with paginator.count

verification.instructions: Run the view and check Django debug toolbar or logs to verify only one COUNT query is executed

subtasks.notes: Successfully replaced materials.count() with paginator.count on line 49 of apps/materials/views.py. This eliminates the duplicate COUNT query since the Paginator already executes one internally. Committed as da7aee0.

subtasks.description: Fix supplier_list view - replace suppliers.count() with paginator.count

verification.instructions: Run the view and check Django debug toolbar or logs to verify only one COUNT query is executed

subtasks.notes: Successfully replaced suppliers.count() with paginator.count on line 166 of apps/materials/views.py. This eliminates the duplicate COUNT query since the Paginator already executes one internally. Committed as 5d59e1c.

subtasks.description: Fix quick_print view - remove bins.count() or optimize query

verification.instructions: Run the view and verify query count. Since bins are limited to 100, consider if total count is actually needed.

subtasks.notes: Successfully optimized quick_print view by replacing bins.count() with len(bins_list) after evaluating the queryset slice. This eliminates the duplicate COUNT query since we're already limiting results to 100. The queryset is evaluated once using list(bins[:100]) and then len() is used for counting, which doesn't trigger any additional database queries. Committed as 2aba0b0.

parallelism.speedup_estimate: Sequential execution recommended for simple optimization

acceptance_criteria: Each list view executes only one COUNT query instead of two
Total count displayed in UI remains accurate
No functional changes to pagination behavior

verification_steps.name: Manual Query Verification
verification_steps.command: Check Django debug toolbar or enable query logging
verification_steps.expected_outcome: One COUNT query per list view instead of two

verification_steps.name: UI Verification
verification_steps.command: Load each affected list view in browser
verification_steps.expected_outcome: Total counts display correctly, pagination works normally

verification_strategy.reasoning: Low risk performance optimization - no functional changes, only query optimization

checks: Verify COUNT query reduction using Django debug toolbar
Confirm 50-100ms performance improvement per view on large datasets
